findings.title: New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public SPI that third parties can implement. This PR adds `int order();` as an abstract method with no default. Any existing out-of-tree implementation will no longer compile or load (AbstractMethodError) after upgrading. The method should have a default (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve binary/source compatibility.

findings.title: Multiple crypto providers silently resolved by unstable order tie
findings.body: detectProvider() previously failed when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by order() reversed and picks the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath containing e.g. both default and FIPS providers ties and the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath order (stable sort preserves input order). This can silently run non-FIPS crypto in a FIPS deployment instead of failing fast.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, e.g. SUN/JKS provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers use this method to obtain BC-specific algorithms. Returning an arbitrary JCA provider is semantically wrong and will cause NoSuchAlgorithm or wrong-provider behavior; like WildFlyElytronProvider it should return null or throw UnsupportedOperationException.

findings.title: DER decoder accepts indefinite-length encoding and trailing data
findings.body: readLength() explicitly returns -1 for 0x80 indefinite-length encoding, which DER forbids, and readSequence() loops `while (length > 0)` without rejecting negative remainder or trailing bytes after the SEQUENCE. Malformed/crafted ECDSA signatures can therefore be accepted or mis-parsed instead of rejected by the authz-client signature conversion path.

findings.title: Oversized ECDSA integers silently truncated instead of rejected
findings.body: integerToBytes() used by asn1derToConcatenatedRS() truncates to the last qLength bytes when `bytes.length > qLength`. An r or s value larger than the curve size (e.g. more than qLength+1 bytes) should be rejected as an invalid signature, but here high-order bytes are silently dropped, masking invalid signatures and weakening signature validation.

findings.title: ES384/ES512 tests reuse a P-256 key and prove nothing
findings.body: The test generates one key with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (default P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512, only varying the requested concatenated length. Converting a P-256 DER signature to 96/132-byte concatenations and back round-trips trivially but never exercises real P-384/P-521 keys, real signature sizes, or verification with Signature.verify, so bugs in those curves would not be caught.
